This method extracts a topologically correct isosurface from a binary volumetric image by defining the surface geometry through valid foreground-background connectivity couples $(\alpha, \lambda)$ [S1].

The claim states that the method extracts a topologically correct isosurface from a binary volumetric image by defining surface geometry through valid foreground-background connectivity couples $( eta,  lambda)$. Source [S1] explicitly defines 'valid connectedness couple' as a pair $( eta,  lambda)$ where $ eta$ is foreground connectivity and $ lambda$ is background connectivity. It lists the valid couples as (26, 6), (18, 6), (6, 26), and (6, 18). The source further states that the isosurface is defined based on these valid couples (Definition 8) and proves that for any valid couple, the resulting surface is an oriented two-dimensional combinatorial manifold without boundary (Theorem 5), which implies topological correctness. The source also confirms the method works on binary volumetric images (binary picture I) and is used for segmentation of medical images (volumetric data).
